newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 4.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday. IRISH TIMES - A majority of voters - 65 percent - wants the abortion issue to be resolved by another referendum, a poll carried out by the Irish Times/MRBI shows. - Government parties have seized on the disarray within the potential Fianna Fail/ Progressive Democrat coalition over water charges to launch a pre-election attack on the proposed alternative government. - A flood of cash from booming tax revenues will generate an extra 400 million Irish pounds for the Exchequer, giving the government more room to manoeuvre in the Budget and helping to cut borrowing. IRISH INDEPENDENT - Secondhand house prices have soared by a fifth in the Dublin area over the last year and the boom shows no sign of slackening, Central Bank figures indicate. - Support for Fianna Fail among Dublin constituencies has fallen by eight percentage points - from 44 percent to 36 percent - a new political poll shows. EXAMINER - A 27-year-old Mayo woman found dead in western Australia is believed to have been the latest victim of a serial killer who stalks the night-club district of Perth. - Ryanair has drawn the wrath of travel agents after cutting commission, with Irish travel agents set to join UK tour operators in breaking off relations with the company. - With Irish inflation and residential mortgage lending under control, interest rates could be lower by the end of the year, a leading Irish economist has predicted.
